hook.line: Every morning Hernando walks into the café and Tomás greets him the Bogotá way. To Vale, two minutes later, he just says *ven*. Same idea, two shapes: it depends on who's at the door.

rule:
You now have three ways to tell someone what to do.

A friend, someone you call *tú*: the he/she form. *mira*, *espera*, *come*. Plus the eight short ones: *ven*, *ten*, *pon*, *sal*, *haz*, *di*, *ve*, *sé*.

Someone you call *usted*: swap the vowel. *mire*, *espere*, *coma*. The odd verbs build on the I form: *venga*, *tenga*, *ponga*, *salga*, *haga*, *diga*.

A group: the *usted* form plus *n*. *miren*, *esperen*, *vengan*.

Don't choose fresh each time. Use whatever you already say to that person: if Hernando is *usted* in your questions, he's *usted* in your commands too. And don't mix inside one sentence.

A Bogotá extra: *¡Siga!* means "come in" or "go ahead", not just "keep going".
smallPrint: Teachers call these the *tú*, *usted* and *ustedes* forms of the imperative.

options: The lady pays with the card.
Go on two blocks, Vale. (to a friend)
Put the card here, sir. (to a friend)
Put the card here, Tomás. (to a friend)

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *Mira* or *Mire* and type the whole sentence: *___ esto, señora.*
Pick *ven* or *venga* and type the whole sentence. You're talking to your friend Vale: *Vale, ___ mañana temprano.*
yourTurn.why: Vale is *tú*, so the short form: *ven*.

yourTurn.prompt: Tell a friend: Wait a moment.
yourTurn.why: For a friend, the he/she form: *espera*.

yourTurn.prompt: Tell a stranger (formal): Wait a moment.
Say it to Hernando, whom you call *usted*: *Ten, es para ti.*
Say it to Vale, your friend, instead of a stranger: *Salga temprano.*
yourTurn.why: *Salir* is one of the eight short ones: *sal*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it to the whole table at once: *Come algo.*
yourTurn.why: A group gets the *usted* shape plus *n*: *coman*.

pitfalls.why: Almost. Pick one and stay with it: *usted* all the way, *venga* and *mire*.
*Tiene* is "she has". Handing something over to *usted* is *tenga*.
If you call him *señor*, he's *usted*, so it's *siga*.

personal: Think of someone you call *tú* and someone you'd call *usted*. Write one instruction for each, about something you'd really ask them to do.
